correctness.rationale: The endpoint reflection gives cyclic Jacobi blocks; their first-coordinate Krylov determinants are independent of w because the subdiagonals are fixed. The direct-sum Krylov determinant differs from their monic cross-resultant by a nonzero constant. The Fourier modes split into a shared pair for each nonzero double eigenvalue, with only the symmetric zero mode unshared in the symmetric block; the even-order alternating mode is antisymmetric. Varying w changes the first antisymmetric diagonal by 2(w−1). The trailing minor does not vanish at a shared eigenvalue, so each contributes one linear factor. The continuant at zero gives det A(w) = 1+(n−1)w in odd order and twice that in even order, including the smallest orders. The open-path triangular Krylov determinant determines the sign; polynomial identity on the real line also gives the complex extension. The rank at w=1 counts the distinct eigenvalues with nonzero endpoint projections. For fixed n the r vanishing singular values are each O(|w−1|); the exact determinant order r and the nonvanishing other singular values force matching lower bounds on each. The smallest real Gramian eigenvalue is its squared singular value. The uploaded checker was inspected, not executed; its finite reported tests are not the basis for the all-n result.
